newsitem.title: ITALY: Euro would be more stable than lira - Consob.
newsitem.headline: Euro would be more stable than lira - Consob.

text.p: The single European currency would be more stable than the lira, although the Italian currency has proved its strength since returning to the exchange rate mechanism (ERM), Tommaso Padoa Schioppa, chairman of Italian stock market regulator Consob, said.

He was replying to a question during a forum on "The euro and globalization of financial markets: prospects for Italy" as part of the Global 24 international conference on the impact of European monetary union.
"The lira has stood up to the test of stability since its re-entry (to the ERM in November 1996)," Padoa Schioppa said.
He added: "the euro will be more stable than the lira and (for European countries) there will be less risk of losing competitiveness through exchange rate fluctuations."

He said he saw the euro winning space on the international markets. "Today the dollar dominates, but it is probable that the euro will occupy more room than that taken up today by all the European currencies put together," he added.
